subject: Pathway Labs pilot: request for short-lived dedicated slice + autoscale exception
messages:
From: Sara Connors <sara@pathwaylabs.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 12 Jan 2026 09:15:00 -0800
Subject: Pilot capacity ask — low-latency reserved slice for 3-week pilot

Hi Marissa,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team at Pathway Labs is excited to move forward with a short pilot. Our key ask: a reserved dedicated slice (GPU pool) for a 3-week window to validate sub-50ms P99 inference latency under realistic traffic. We expect a steady 40 qps during peak hours with occasional spikes to ~120 qps for short runs.

We understand this is non-standard, but for our compliance review and demo commitments we need guaranteed capacity (not just best-effort burst). I've attached an initial traffic profile and requested capacity worksheet. Can you confirm whether Redwood can provide a temporary reserved lane with an autoscale exception for the pilot window, and any cost/contract implications?

High-level timeline: pilot start target Feb 2 — Feb 22.

Thanks,
Sara
Sara Connors
Head of Platform
Pathway Labs

Attachment: pathway_capacity_request_v1.xlsx (spreadsheet, 18KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>
To: Sara Connors <sara@pathwaylabs.com>
Cc: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 13 Jan 2026 10:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — low-latency reserved slice for 3-week pilot

Sara — thanks for the note and the worksheet. Looping in Kimberly (Capacity & Commercial), Jonas (Infra), and Laura (Product Ops) to evaluate.

Quick answers up front:
- We can offer temporary reserved capacity for the requested window, but we need to scope the exact GPU VM count and a short SLA addendum for reserved lanes.
- An autoscale exception (temporary higher burst ceiling) is possible but requires an approval and a short OSS (ops/safety) checklist.
- Costing: we'll propose a fixed pilot carve (monthly-equivalent pro-rated) + overage for sustained spikes.

Kimberly/Jonas/Laura — can you review the attached spreadsheet and confirm what minimal slice configuration meets Pathway's latency target and whether an autoscale-exception approval is plausible for Feb 2 start? If we can't hit Feb 2 we should propose the soonest available window.

I'll prep a one-page mutual action plan and a draft SLA addendum once we have the technical sizing.

—Marissa
Marissa Cole
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference

From: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 14 Jan 2026 08:30:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — short notes on sizing and exceptions

Marissa/Sara — looked through the worksheet. High-level notes:

1) Sizing: for sub-50ms P99 at 40 qps steady with occasional 120 qps spikes, we should provision a slice equivalent to 8x A100-80G-ish instances with continuous batching enabled and prefix caching for hot keys. That gives predictable latency headroom and keeps autoscale churn low.

2) Autoscale exception: Ops will accept a timeboxed exception, but we require:
   - A runbook (2 pages) for spike scenarios and kill-switch thresholds.
   - A brief security attestation that no sensitive keys are being cached in plaintext (Pathway to confirm).
   - A refundable pilot deposit covering the pro-rated reserved charge + 25% buffer for overage.

3) Availability: Our earliest contiguous window with that slice footprint is Feb 9–Mar 1. We can consider Feb 2 if Pathway accepts a smaller baseline (6x instances) + guaranteed spike window and explicit risk acceptance.

4) Commercial/contract: Laura — we need a short SLA addendum for reserved lanes + a one-time pilot amendment. I'll attach a redline template (SLA_addendum_draft.docx) to send to legal once commercial terms are agreed.

Action items:
- Jonas: validate capacity placement (us-west vs us-east) and pre-warm time estimate.
- Laura: draft the pilot amendment and deposit/payment terms.
- Marissa: confirm if Pathway can accept Feb 9 or will they take reduced baseline for Feb 2.

Kimberly Park
Head, Capacity & Commercial
Redwood Inference

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.ai>
To: Kimberly Park <kimberly_park@redwood.ai>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>, Aditya Rao <aditya_rao@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Jan 2026 17:42:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Pilot capacity ask — placement and ops notes

Quick infra update after sizing run and capacity check:

- Placement: recommend us-west1 for the pilot (proximity to Pathway endpoints + available pre-warm inventory). If Pathway needs EU, we can mirror but with longer lead times.
- Pre-warm: 24–36 hours to warm KV caches and validate pipeline; plan a 48-hour buffer before live demo.
- Safety: we'll require the runbook Kimberly mentioned and an on-call alignment for the first 48 hours of live traffic (ops rotation).
- If Pathway agrees to Feb 9 start we can lock the slice on Feb 5 and complete the pre-warm by Feb 7.

I'll start a short ops checklist in the shared doc and post an initial slot reservation in the capacity calendar (JIRA:INFRA-9812).

Jonas Weber
Senior Infrastructure Manager
Redwood Inference
